Engine oil lubricates and cools the engine\'s moving parts. It degrades with distance and with time — even when the car mostly sits.
A little while, yes. But running long past the interval accelerates engine wear — the most expensive damage a routine service can prevent.
Front and rear tires wear at different rates. Rotating them evens out the wear so the set lasts longer and grips predictably.
Briefly, yes — but uneven wear compounds. Skipped rotations can cut thousands of kilometres from a tire set\'s life.
Pads, discs and brake fluid wear gradually. An inspection catches thinning pads before they start damaging the discs.
Not if you hear grinding or feel vibration when braking. Worn pads quickly ruin discs and multiply the repair cost — brakes are not a wait-and-see system.
Car batteries age chemically, typically lasting 3–5 years. Cold mornings and lots of short trips age them faster.
Usually it warns you first — slow cranking on cold starts. If yours is past 4 years, have it tested before winter rather than waiting for a no-start.
The engine air filter keeps dust out of the combustion chambers. A clogged filter chokes airflow.
Yes, for a while — a dirty filter costs fuel economy and performance long before it causes any damage.
Filters the air you breathe inside the car — pollen, dust and soot.
Yes — there\'s no mechanical risk. But a saturated filter means weak airflow, windows that fog up, and musty smells.
Transmission fluid lubricates and cools the gearbox. It degrades slowly and is the easiest interval to forget.
You can schedule ahead, but don\'t skip it — old fluid is a leading cause of transmission failure, one of the costliest repairs on any car.
Coolant carries heat away from the engine and prevents corrosion inside it. Its protective additives wear out over the years.
Short-term, yes. Long-term, degraded coolant corrodes the radiator and water pump from the inside out.
Spark plugs ignite the fuel. Worn plugs misfire, waste fuel, and strain the ignition coils.
For a while — but severely worn plugs can take the much pricier ignition coils with them.
The timing belt keeps the engine\'s rotating parts synchronized. It\'s rubber — it ages whether you drive or not.
This is the one interval never to gamble on. If the belt snaps, the engine destroys itself in seconds. Replace it on schedule.
Wiper rubber hardens and splits with sun and frost, usually within a year or two.
Only until the first heavy rain at night. Streaking wipers are a visibility risk, and the fix takes minutes.
Your policy has a fixed expiry date, and driving uninsured is illegal in most places.
No. A lapse can void claims, bring fines, and raise your future premiums.
Vehicle registration must be renewed on the schedule set by your local authority.
No — driving on expired registration risks fines and can complicate insurance claims.
Periodic technical inspection verifies the car is roadworthy and legal to drive.
Only until the deadline. Driving past it usually means fines, and it can void insurance cover.
Emissions testing checks that the exhaust system meets legal limits.
Only until the deadline — an expired certificate carries the same legal risk as a failed one.

Smart car maintenance reminders, fuel tracking & cost analytics

AutoMinder helps you track vehicle maintenance, mileage, fuel, and service records without an account.

Key Features:
• Maintenance reminders with date and odometer triggers
• Clear overdue, due soon, snoozed, completed, and unknown states
• Service history with costs, notes, workshops, and mileage
• Fuel logs with spending and efficiency trends
• Multiple vehicle support
• Home screen widget for quick maintenance status
• Offline-first core tracking
• CSV service-history sharing
• Dark mode and Material Design
• Optional Pro upgrade for premium features and an ad-free experience
